name: juhyeonni
description: Juhyeon Lee's personal Claude Code plugin marketplace — skills and agents I build to work more efficiently.

plugins.name: annotated-ui-pdf
plugins.description: Screenshot a web app and produce a PDF that outlines chosen UI elements with numbered boxes and short captions. A general-purpose visual explainer for release notes, bug reports, design/QA review, how-to guides, and design specs. Needs a Playwright MCP and a headless Chrome/Chromium/Edge.

plugins.name: clear-draft
plugins.description: Ask for the missing inputs first, then write the draft. Writing fails on missing input, not on prose skill — so this diagnoses seven slots (deliverable, outcome, audience, key sentence, evidence, ask, constraints), asks at most four questions per round through AskUserQuestion, declares the one-line BLUF and a length budget before drafting, then writes conclusion-first (C-C-C) with a pre-submit self-check. Covers Slack/chat messages, GitHub issues, PR descriptions, emails, design docs, bug reports, and papers.

plugins.name: macro-loop
plugins.description: A regular routine for AI-assisted development on GitHub Issues: triage, grill, spec, implement, open a PR, and verify in a fresh context. Each stage can be the entry point; a missing input warns instead of blocking, and a skipped stage is recorded on the Issue as a skipped:* label so it can be counted later. Works in local and cloud Claude Code sessions through the GitHub REST API. Skills are forked from mattpocock/skills (MIT).

plugins.name: macro-loop-band
plugins.description: A band above the Claude Code prompt with one row per Issue the session's macro-loop skills touched: how far along it is, whose turn it is, what to do next, and links to its spec, PR and verdict. Needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later; drawn in the terminal and the desktop app only.

plugins.name: red-team
plugins.description: Adversarially review a document or code diff as a specific persona — a target reader or user with real knowledge gaps. The review runs in a fresh-eyes subagent with a separate context from the author, so it catches the blind spots the writer cannot see. Returns severity-ranked findings, each with its location, the persona’s reaction, and a concrete fix, plus an honest PASS / NEEDS-FIX verdict. Personas are reusable inline, per-project, or from memory. Supports a review → fix → re-review loop, and an integrated mode that checks whole-document consistency (contradictions, duplication, broken cross-references, terminology).
